content:
While iOS 27 is clearly the focus of preview software, Apple is still preparing its next iPhone system update, iOS 26.6. Apple has released the fifth developer beta of iOS 26.6. The iOS 26.6 beta has been in testing since late May.

iOS 26.6 features and changes

So far, we have discovered two noteworthy changes in the iOS 26.6 beta.

First, there is an adjustment to the maximum number of contacts that can be blocked. Second, what appears to be an all-new iPhone anti-theft feature is in development.

This update may also be laying the groundwork for Spotlight indexing on iPhone and iPad, to be used by Siri AI in iOS 27.

Given that attention has shifted to iOS 27, we do not expect any other major new features or changes.

Apple's next major system update will be released to users in September, and Apple will continue to refine iOS 27 throughout the summer.

iOS 26.6 will be the next version to be officially released, following iOS 26 which launched last fall and its subsequent updates.

Last year, the first beta of iOS 18.6 came out after the first beta of iOS 26. This means iOS 26.6 is running slightly ahead of Apple's 2025 release schedule.

9to5Mac perspective

With iOS 26.6 releasing its fifth beta today, it is likely that iOS 26.6 will be publicly released by the end of July. We may first see a release candidate along with release notes, with the official release coming about a week later.

Meanwhile, iOS 27 remains the focus of the next major update. We expect the first public beta to be released as early as this week, with the fourth developer beta likely arriving next week.

iOS 27 will not officially launch outside of its preview testing cycle until September. For non-testers, iOS 26.5 is currently in use, and iOS 26.6 will accompany most users until the fall.
